newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat price seen stable at higher level.
newsitem.headline: German wheat price seen stable at higher level.

text.p: German wheat prices are expected to stay at higher levels reached amid recent export business although follow-on orders have not been seen yet, brokers said on Wednesday.
"The market has gone quiet this week after demand from French exporters and eastern Europe lifted prices, but European competitors are now beginning to look cheaper," one said.

The Hamburg grain exchange this week raised its bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) by 2.50 marks to 277.50 marks a tonne free Hamburg and the spot feed wheat price was also 2.50 marks higher at 272.50.
Fob Baltic sellers were quoting 280-295 marks for March delivery 12 percent wheat, 2.50-7.50 marks more than last week, but added this was mostly nominal.
March material with 13/14 percent protein was in a 287.50-307.50 marks range, up 2.50-5.00, depending on shipment sizes.
March fob barley in small shipment sizes was steady around 260-275 marks, with a new quote in the 25,000 tonne size at 280 marks.
Traders said new Saudi export business next month could lift prices.
They also reported some barley sales to Denmark.
Fob rye sellers were little changed at 262.50-267.50 marks.
